tasks.short: Turn board and Finance Director budget guidelines into budget rules, templates and instructions for site and cost-centre managers.

steps.what: Read the budget directive and list what it changes in current budget policy

loop.input: budget directive (board letter, CAO wage round, bank covenant terms) and the current budget policy on SharePoint
loop.output: list of affected policy clauses and budget parameters, each with a quote from the source paragraph
loop.check: every item must cite a paragraph that exists in the source; parameters must map to a known field in the parameter table; the analyst ticks each item
loop.stop: one pass plus one retry on failed citations; anything uncited goes to the analyst as an open question
loop.why_not_simpler: directives arrive as free text in Dutch and English with no fixed structure, so rules alone cannot find which clauses they touch

steps.what: Work out the effect on site and cost-centre budgets in Excel
Write the budget instruction and update manager templates

loop.input: approved change list, impact table and last year's instruction
loop.output: draft instruction in Dutch with changed sections marked; templates regenerated from the parameter table by code
loop.check: every number in the text is pulled from the impact table by a script and compared; tracked changes against last year shown to the analyst
loop.stop: one draft; failed number check blocks the draft and returns it to the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: the explanatory text for managers changes each year; the templates and numbers themselves are pure code

steps.what: Agree the policy with Controller and Finance Director and sign off
Publish on SharePoint, mail managers and answer their questions

tasks.design: Keep budget parameters (wage increase from the CAO, flex caps, cost ceilings per site) in one versioned parameter table on a governed data platform instead of scattered Excel tabs. Code recalculates the impact on every cost centre and regenerates the manager templates; a small model loop reads new directives and drafts the change list and instruction text, which the analyst approves before a Power Automate flow publishes to SharePoint and notifies managers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget rules lived in people's heads and in last year's Excel files, so each directive meant manual re-reading and re-keying; free-text directives could not be parsed by rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a parameter-driven budget model cheap to build, and models can now reliably extract and cite clauses from a directive when every claim is checked against the source.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding how a vague directive should apply to a specific site or the flex pool is judgement and negotiation; parameters must first be defined and agreed, which is organisational work, not software.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the board actually means, where site managers will pad or push back, and what the Finance Director will accept.

ambition.what: Re-issue budget rules each quarter when CAO, fuel or volume assumptions move, instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops re-keying templates and spends the time defining parameters and settling disputes with site managers; they gain ownership of the budget parameter table, with sign-off staying with the Finance Director.

reach.task: Maintaining the chart of accounts and cost-centre structure in AFAS
reach.learn: How cost centres map to budget lines so parameter changes land in the right place.

reach.task: Translating CAO wage rounds into salary cost assumptions
reach.learn: The CAO increment and allowance rules that drive the largest budget parameter.

evidence.claim: Finance executives rate AI as more useful than expected for budgeting (net +42), the strongest of all tasks surveyed.
Speeding up budgets without defined drivers and encoded policies makes existing errors harder to catch.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor, so drafting must run on a governed platform.
A model can extract and cite clauses from a policy-type document when citations are checked mechanically.

assumptions: Directives arrive a few times a year plus ad-hoc changes, not daily.
Budget templates are Excel files per cost centre on SharePoint.
A governed data platform or at least a managed SQL store is available or will be set up for FP&A.
unknowns: How many cost centres and budget templates exist per site.
Whether the board directive is written down or given verbally to the Finance Director.
Whether Noordhaven has an approved enterprise model service for confidential finance documents.
research_questions: How much of last year's budget instruction changed versus the year before; if under 20 percent, is a drafting loop worth it?
Can all current budget rules be written as parameters in one table, or do many depend on site-specific exceptions?
Do site managers actually read the instruction, or do questions come in by mail regardless?

tasks.short: Build cost-benefit cases for investments, financing and operating choices, such as forklift lease versus buy or flex versus own staff.

steps.what: Take the request and gather costs from AFAS, agency invoices and supplier quotes

loop.input: supplier quote and lease offer PDFs
loop.output: line items with amounts, terms, interest rate and duration in a fixed schema
loop.check: extracted lines must sum to the quote total; missing fields are flagged; ledger and agency data come by code, not by the model
loop.stop: one extraction plus one retry; if totals do not tie the analyst keys the quote by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: quotes from lessors, banks and equipment suppliers have no common format

steps.what: Build the model: NPV, payback, cash effect and scenarios
Test assumptions and sensitivities with the requester and site manager
Write the recommendation memo with options for the Finance Director

loop.input: model outputs, scenario table and agreed assumptions
loop.output: memo with two or three options, their numbers, risks and open points; no single answer forced
loop.check: a script matches every figure in the memo to the model output; the analyst writes the recommendation line
loop.stop: one draft and one regeneration; a failed figure check blocks release
loop.why_not_simpler: the narrative changes per case; the figures and charts are generated by code

tasks.design: A standard cost-benefit template in Python on the governed data platform, with fixed rules for discount rate, depreciation, tax and CAO labour cost, fed by scheduled pulls of the AFAS ledger and agency hours and invoices. A bounded model loop extracts supplier and lease quotes and drafts the options memo; Power BI shows scenarios to the requester, and the Finance Director decides.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each case was a new Excel build because data came from three systems and PDF quotes, and there was no agreed template for discount rate or labour cost.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a reusable, tested template and data pulls cheap; models extract varied quotes well when totals are checked.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing assumptions such as volume growth or a client contract renewal, and dealing with requesters who want a given answer.
tasks.human_edge: Challenging optimistic assumptions from site managers and judging strategic value the numbers miss, such as client retention or safety.

ambition.what: Run a cost-benefit check on every flex-versus-own-staff choice per site each season, not only on large investments.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time building spreadsheets and more time questioning assumptions; they gain the right to set the standard assumptions in the template, while the Finance Director keeps the decision.

reach.task: Setting depreciation and lease accounting treatment (IFRS 16 or Dutch GAAP)
reach.learn: How a choice lands in the books so the case matches the later actuals.

reach.task: Planning seasonal flex and permanent staffing per site
reach.learn: Which non-cost factors (CAO rules, retention, training) make own staff better or worse than agency workers.

evidence.claim: Finance executives report net +27 for model building and +26 for scenario planning as more useful than expected.
FP&A products already gather data, run scenario mechanics and draft commentary while people decide on capital.
Copilot in Power BI needs a prepared semantic model and does not officially support non-English use.
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%).

assumptions: Roughly two to four cost-benefit cases per month across the three sites.
Agency hours and invoices can be exported from all three agency portals.
Noordhaven has agreed a discount rate or can set one.
unknowns: Whether the agency portals offer an API or only CSV exports.
Which financing options Rabobank and lessors usually offer and in what format.
Whether hourly flex data contains personal data that would need works-council consent to process.
research_questions: Do the last ten business cases share enough structure to fit one template?
How often did the realised cost differ from the case by more than 10 percent, and why?
Can quote extraction tie totals on 9 of 10 historical quotes?

tasks.short: Look for ways to cut cost or raise margin, such as agency overbilling, overtime, idle hours or unprofitable customers.

steps.what: Pull data and scan cost centres and customers for unusual cost or margin
Dig into candidates with site and operations managers
Size the saving or margin gain
Write the proposal and track whether savings are realised

loop.output: one-page proposal with options and owners
loop.check: figures matched to the estimate by script; the analyst edits and approves
loop.stop: one draft; failed figure check returns it to the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: proposal wording depends on the case; the tracker itself is a plain Power BI page on the ledger

tasks.design: Replace the ad-hoc Excel digging with scheduled rule checks on the governed data platform: agency invoices versus approved hours and agreed rates, overtime and idle hours per site, cost per pallet and margin per customer. Results appear as a ranked opportunity list in Power BI with a weekly Teams notice; agreed savings are tracked against AFAS actuals on the same dashboard.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency, hours and ledger data sat in separate systems joined by hand, so scanning happened only when someone had time or a hunch.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the joins and rule checks quick to build and maintain; the nightly AFAS extract already feeds Power BI.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing whether an outlier is waste or a reason, such as a peak client order; getting site managers to act; defining cost per pallet consistently across sites.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from the floor why a cost is high and persuading a site manager to change practice.

ambition.what: A monthly margin-per-customer review for the commercial team, which today gets no such view.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops hunting in spreadsheets and spends the time with site managers on the top five items; they gain the right to put opportunities on the monthly management agenda.

reach.learn: Which invoice mismatches recur so the rule checks can stop them before payment, not after.
Which customers combine low margin with late payment, a stronger case for repricing.

evidence.claim: The least successful AI finance tasks are those that demand human judgement.
FP&A agent products flag records that do not tie and monitor for changes.
Faster reports invite more reports; AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting.
Hours data tied to named workers is personal data under the AVG and needs care.

assumptions: Agency contracts state hourly rates and markups that can be put in a rate table.
AFAS holds cost per site and per customer at a usable level.
Analysis is done at site and team level, not per named worker.
unknowns: Whether the works council must consent because overtime and hours checks could be used to monitor individual employees (WOR art. 27).
Whether revenue is booked per customer in AFAS or only in total.
How much agency overbilling has been found before, if any.
research_questions: Run the agency rate check on last year's invoices: does it find more than the cost of building it?
Can cost per pallet be defined the same way at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?
Of past savings ideas, how many were acted on, and what stopped the rest?

role.altitude: From assembling budgets, cases and scans in Excel to owning the budget parameters, case assumptions and opportunity rules, and spending the freed time with the Finance Director and site managers.
reach: controller: cost-centre structure and accounting treatment, so models match the books
cnb: CAO wage rounds as the main labour cost driver
hrbp: seasonal flex versus own staff planning per site
bookkeeper: agency invoice checks before payment
skills_to_grow: Defining drivers and parameters in a versioned table
Reading and testing Python or SQL pipelines on the data platform
Preparing a Power BI semantic model so Copilot answers correctly
Challenging assumptions and presenting options rather than one answer
AVG and works-council basics for hours and headcount data
role.ambitious_version: Monthly rolling forecasts and scenarios per site, driven by agreed volume, CAO and flex drivers, with every investment and flex choice checked against a standard case template and savings tracked to actuals.
